From: Ari Mann <ari@nimblpilot.com>

Date: Thu, 30 May 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing inquiry — NimbusPilot fleet thermostat

Hi Stephanie,

We're kicking off capacity planning for a new product line at NimbusPilot ("Conductor") and are evaluating reserved GPU capacity to meet deterministic latency for inference. We're interested in Redwood Dedicated and want to get a realistic sizing estimate early in the procurement cycle.

High level: Conductor will power multimodal assistant sessions (text+short audio snippets) for enterprise customers. We're expecting a phased rollout, but need a plan for the initial GA footprint. A few quick context points:
- Expect steady background traffic from 04:00-20:00 PT with short nightly troughs.
- Early pilot (Q3) target: 20k daily active sessions, peak 1,200 concurrent sessions during regional peak.
- Typical prompt tokens: ~110 tokens; typical model completion 210 tokens. We plan to use an LlamaX-70B quantized variant.
- Session behavior: individual sessions typically consist of 3-8 turns; many sessions are short-lived (<60s) but a small portion (~6%) persist with streaming for longer conversations.

Can you share your pre-sales questionnaire or a set of required telemetry fields so we can send a sample traffic dump? Also any short checklist for SLAs you recommend (p99 latency target, fallback model options, storage/kv retention) would be helpful.

Thanks,
Ari Mann
CTO, NimbusPilot
ari@nimblpilot.com

P.S. attaching high-level product brief in a follow-up (will send CSV sample of minute-level RPS distribution).

Hi Ari,

Thanks for the context — this is exactly the level of detail we need to start. I attached a short "fleet thermostat" questionnaire that surfaces the specific telemetry and constraints our sizing engine uses. If you can fill the short form and attach a minute-level RPS sample (CSV) we'll produce a preliminary GPU footprint estimate within 3 business days.

Key fields that speed evaluation:
- Peak concurrent sessions and how you define concurrency (open session vs. active token generation)
- Prompt and response token distributions (P50/P95/P99) or example prompt/response pairs
- Expected sustained vs. burst windows (minutes and expected scale factor)
- Session affinity / KV cache reuse: percent of requests that reuse a cached prefix
- Target latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99) and acceptable tail degradation/fallback rules
- Start date for reserved capacity and desired commitment term (monthly/annual)

Attachments: fleet_thermostat_questionnaire.pdf (short form), example CSV template included.

I'll loop in Marissa (solutions) and Ben (capacity) once you return the data so we can align a committed-plan recommendation + pricing.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the quick reply. We've filled the questionnaire and attached a minute-level RPS sample (nimbus_traffic_sample.csv). Key answers inline:
- Peak concurrent sessions (open-session definition): 1,200 (regional peak, US west)
- Active token-gen concurrency (approx): 420 concurrent token-generation pipelines at peak
- Prompt token distribution (P50/P95/P99): 95 / 140 / 210
- Completion token distribution (P50/P95/P99): 175 / 260 / 420
- Burst windows: 10-18 minute micro-bursts 2-3x baseline; predictable daily peak at 11:00 PT and 16:00 PT
- KV cache reuse: approx 28% prefix reuse across sessions during same user interactions
- Target latency: p95 <= 450ms for short-turn interactions (<=250 tokens). For long-form streaming we accept p95 <= 1.2s. p99 target: <=1.8s (we're flexible if fallbacks are defined)
- Start date desired for reserved fleet: 2029-09-01 (pilot), GA 2029-11-15
- Commitment: prefer 12-month with staged ramp (pilot -> GA -> scale)

Attachments: nimbus_traffic_sample.csv (minute-level RPS, 14 days)

Let me know if you need any more breakdowns (per-region, user cohort).

Best,
Ari
CTO, NimbusPilot
